clue.text: Jack affected enthusiasm for meeting

parts.note: J is the abbreviation for jack in a pack of cards
unction is gushing, insincere earnestness

explanation.surface: Someone puts on a show of keenness to get through a dull meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: A junction is a place where roads or lines come together, so a point of joining.

clue.text: Things thrown out of planes above America

parts.note: jets are aircraft
AM is an abbreviation for America

explanation.surface: Objects are dropped from aircraft flying over the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'above' puts the first piece over the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Jetsam is cargo or gear cast overboard to lighten a ship, so goods deliberately discarded.

clue.text: Stingy monarch? Not so far!

parts.note: near is an old word for mean with money
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a king is a miser, and is told he has not gone far.
explanation.definitionFit: Nearer is the comparative of near, meaning at a smaller distance, so closer.

clue.text: Sort of course may lead here

definitions.meaning: first meaning: somewhat, to some extent

definitions.note: a place reached, rather than a phrase meaning 'here'
definitions.meaning: second meaning: where a university course ends, at a qualification

explanation.walkthrough: 'Sort of course' reads as a kind of course; split it after 'Sort of', and the course is a degree course.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means somewhat or partly, and literally a university course leads a student toward a qualification.

clue.text: Draught beer may be free from danger

definitions.meaning: first meaning: beer served straight from the wooden cask
second meaning: the idiom for being clear of trouble

explanation.surface: Beer on tap might turn out to be safe to drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Draught beer is drawn from the barrel, and the idiom means past difficulty, like walkers emerging from a forest.

clue.text: King with an elite group of men serving the state

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
taken as written
the Special Air Service, the British army's elite regiment

explanation.surface: A monarch and a crack military unit go off to serve their country.
explanation.definitionFit: Kansas is one of the fifty United States, so a state in the American sense.

clue.text: Affair with a man like Othello reported

indicators.note: a report is spoken, so the phrase is judged by its sound

parts.note: Othello is Shakespeare's Moor of Venice

explanation.surface: Gossip spreads about an affair with a jealous man like Shakespeare's Othello.
explanation.definitionFit: Amour is a love affair, especially a secret or illicit one.

clue.text: Incentive from university to inhabit inferior housing it's put up

indicators.note: in a down clue putting something up turns it bottom to top, so it reads backwards
inhabiting a place means living inside it, so these letters go within another word

parts.note: slums are squalid, run-down dwellings
taken as written
U is the abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: A university is spurred to move into poor housing that has been built.
explanation.walkthrough: Both inserts go into the housing word, one after its first letter and one before its last, and the whole is then read bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: A stimulus is something that rouses action or effort, which is what an incentive does.

clue.text: Shanty was first restrained

parts.note: a shanty is a crude hut
to lead is to be in front

explanation.surface: A sea song was the first to be sung, restrained in style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shanty' suggests a sailors' song; here it is a rough hut.
explanation.definitionFit: Shackled means chained or held back, so prevented from free movement.

clue.text: Try a tape out for afternoon entertainment

indicators.note: something put out of order is disturbed, so the letters before it are jumbled

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is told to test a recording to provide some light entertainment after lunch.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea party is a social gathering with tea and cakes, usually held in the afternoon.

clue.text: Bareback rider shows spirit eager to make a comeback

parts.note: go means energy, dash, spirit

indicators.note: coming back means travelling the other way, so the word for keen is read right to left

parts.note: avid means keen

explanation.surface: A horse rider without a saddle shows keen, competitive spirit in a comeback.
explanation.walkthrough: Lady Godiva is said to have ridden naked through Coventry, so 'bareback' describes the rider, not the horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Legend says Lady Godiva rode through the streets of Coventry unclothed, a joking twist on riding without a saddle.

clue.text: I let pope tell about supernatural beings

indicators.note: turned about suggests letters moved around into a different order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone lets the Pope talk about ghosts and spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: The little people are fairies, leprechauns and similar tiny creatures of folklore.

clue.text: Competent to protect English tree

indicators.note: protecting something means surrounding it, so one word is placed around the other

parts.note: able means capable
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A capable person shields a traditional English tree from harm.
explanation.definitionFit: The abele is the white poplar, a European tree with silvery leaves.

clue.text: Bacon, possibly, food for outlaw

parts.note: Roger Bacon, the medieval scholar, was a Franciscan friar
tuck is British slang for food, especially snacks at school

explanation.surface: Bacon, perhaps, is the meal served to a fugitive.
explanation.walkthrough: Bacon looks like breakfast meat beside 'food', but it is the friar Roger Bacon.
explanation.definitionFit: Friar Tuck is one of Robin Hood's band of outlaws in Sherwood Forest.

clue.text: Building work in the Arctic diverted river

indicators.note: something diverted is sent off its course, so the letters are moved into a new order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: Construction near the North Pole has forced a river onto a new course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Diverted river' reads as one phrase, but 'diverted' acts on the Arctic words and the river follows unchanged.
explanation.definitionFit: Architecture is the art and practice of designing and constructing buildings.

clue.text: Red stuff or black rock found round ridge

indicators.note: lying round something means surrounding it, so one word is wrapped about the other

parts.note: coal is a black mineral rock
a chine is a narrow ridge or crest of land

explanation.surface: Geologists find red material or dark stone around a mountain ridge.
explanation.definitionFit: Cochineal is a crimson dye made from crushed insects, used to colour food.

clue.text: Bold, rash king thrown out

indicators.note: someone thrown out is ejected, so a letter is removed from the word for reckless

parts.note: imprudent means unwise or reckless
R is Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A reckless monarch, too daring, is overthrown.
explanation.definitionFit: Impudent means cheeky and disrespectful, the brazen sense of bold.

clue.text: Drink that makes you grow fast

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a cocktail of advocaat and lemonade
second meaning: to increase rapidly, as a rolling ball of packed snow does

explanation.surface: A tonic is promised to make you shoot up quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a party cocktail of advocaat and lemonade, and also a verb for rapid escalation.

clue.text: Wreck one hymn with faults in the instrument

indicators.note: something full of faults is broken, so the letters are reassembled differently

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A hymn is ruined by mistakes in the playing of the instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Instrument' suggests the church organ, but here it is a tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A monkey wrench is an adjustable spanner, a mechanical tool or implement.

clue.text: Inform counsel

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to notify someone of a fact
second meaning: to recommend a course of action

explanation.walkthrough: 'Counsel' looks like a noun for a lawyer, but it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To advise is both to give notice of something and to offer guidance or recommendations.

clue.text: Former church given paint externally becomes bar

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: the external parts of a word are its ends, so only its first and last letters are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of paint

explanation.surface: An old church given an exterior coat of paint is converted into a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' looks like a pub, but it is the preposition meaning apart from.
explanation.definitionFit: Except and bar are both prepositions meaning apart from or excluding, as in 'all bar one'.

clue.text: Poorly cut show is not popular

indicators.note: cutting something shortens it, so the word for ill loses its last letter

parts.note: poorly means ill
to show, or show up, is to arrive

explanation.surface: A badly edited show fails to win over its audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poorly cut' reads as bad editing; in fact 'poorly' is ill and 'cut' trims it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unwelcome is not wanted or received gladly, so it lacks popularity.

clue.text: In the right, I fail to rise

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so a letter sits within the word for a legal claim

parts.note: a lien is a legal right to hold property until a debt is paid
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone admits that, though in the right, they could not get up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the right' reads as being correct; 'the right' is a legal claim and 'In' places the I.
explanation.definitionFit: A lie-in is staying in bed late in the morning, so not getting up at the usual time.

clue.text: Finger pages at back of book sometimes
Ornamental coat sweetheart and lover returned

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its centre, so only the middle letter of sweet is kept

parts.note: the middle letter of sweet

indicators.note: something returned goes back the way it came, so the word for lover is read backwards

parts.note: leman is an old word for a lover

explanation.surface: A fancy jacket is handed back by a sweetheart and lover after a romance ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweetheart' splits into 'sweet' and 'heart'. Leman is an archaic word for a lover or mistress.
explanation.definitionFit: Enamel is a glassy decorative layer fused onto metal or pottery, so a decorative coating.

clue.text: Primate eats little when abroad, resulting in hunger

indicators.note: whatever eats something takes it inside, so one word goes into the other

parts.note: an ape is a primate
petit is French for small

explanation.surface: A monkey that barely eats while travelling overseas ends up starving.
explanation.definitionFit: Appetite is the desire for food, so the same craving as hunger.

clue.text: Army advanced, showing skill

parts.note: the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force
to advance money is to lend it

explanation.surface: An army moves forward and demonstrates its military competence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Advanced' reads as a military push, but it means money handed over as a loan.
explanation.definitionFit: Talent is natural aptitude or ability, the same as skill.

clue.text: He will be given books in set

parts.note: he'll is the contraction of he will
taken as written
NT is the New Testament, a group of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A man will receive a whole set of books as a present.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Books in set' suggests a boxed collection, but 'set' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Hell-bent means determined at any cost, as someone is when firmly set on a plan.
